clue.text: Seeing half of us in streetcar, a shock

indicators.note: in places the half of 'us' inside the word for a streetcar

parts.note: a streetcar is a tram

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is its first letter here

parts.note: first of its two letters

explanation.surface: A passenger is jolted by an encounter on a tram, as if in A Streetcar Named Desire.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of US is U; put it inside TRAM, then add A.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional or physical jolt, a synonym for a shock.

clue.text: Something for the feet has poets dancing

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of 'has poets' moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A footwear item has the poets up and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap shoes are footwear with metal plates on the soles, worn for tap dancing.

clue.text: Bad sprain? I could get you a painkiller

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of 'sprain' plus I are spoilt into a new shape

explanation.surface: A doctor offers a pill for a nasty sprained ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common analgesic drug, an example of a medicine that relieves pain.

clue.text: Make attempt to produce pattern of inlaid veneers

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A craftsman tries to create an inlaid design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' reads as a verb but is a noun: a car make, or MARQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is decorative woodwork made of small pieces of veneer set into furniture.

clue.text: Heard dog barking in Louth town

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters of 'Heard dog' go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hears a dog barking somewhere in County Louth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' seems to describe the dog but is the anagram signal. Louth is a county in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Drogheda is a port town on the River Boyne in County Louth, Ireland: an example of the category.

clue.text: Typical member of parliament

definitions.meaning: first meaning: serving as a characteristic example
second meaning: an elected person who acts for constituents

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an average MP; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Representative is an adjective for typical of a group and a noun for an elected legislator, as in the House of Representatives.

clue.text: Briefly blame head of department in corporation

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: guilt is blame or culpability

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone quickly blames the department chief at a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is an association of tradesmen or merchants, an old sense of corporation as a body of members.

clue.text: Ruler exercises right during Rome uprising

indicators.note: during means the exercises and right come within the other letters
in a down clue, uprising means reading the city's name from the bottom up

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A ruler works out properly while Rome is in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome uprising' reads as a revolt in the city, but in a down clue it turns the name upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, such as Rome, so a kind of ruler.

clue.text: Two articles on composer's third patriotic song

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: an and the are the indefinite and definite articles

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word

parts.note: its third letter

explanation.surface: A composer writes a national song with two articles on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A national anthem is a song of patriotic praise for a country.

clue.text: Fine delicate instrument in black box

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
light means delicate, as in a light touch
a recorder is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A precise, delicate instrument is kept in a black box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' looks like part of the definition but gives RECORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The black box is the popular name for an aircraft's flight data recorder.

clue.text: One can hold things together in examination cut short

parts.note: an exam is often called a paper
to clip is to cut short, as with hair

explanation.surface: Something that binds pages turns up in a shortened exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper clip is a bent wire that holds sheets of paper together, described cryptically here.

clue.text: Deposit on home — enter data

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to deposit something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A notice about paying a deposit on a house, then a command to type in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To input is the computing verb for keying information into a system.

clue.text: Author's metaphor nun grasped, only partly

indicators.note: only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer's figure of speech was understood only in part by a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. E. W. Hornung wrote the Raffles stories.
explanation.definitionFit: E. W. Hornung was the English novelist who created the gentleman thief Raffles.

clue.text: Support back, terribly sore

parts.note: the back of something is its end, as in the back end

indicators.note: terribly shows the letters of 'sore' are badly scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone with a very sore back looks for support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support back' reads as a brace for the spine, but 'back' is END. The rest is SORE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a cause or candidate is to back it publicly, a synonym for supporting it.

clue.text: German painter employed by northern studio

indicators.note: employed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist from Germany works at a studio in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist artist, an instance of the category.

clue.text: Endless delight, of course, making fortune

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a treat is a delight
'Sure!' and 'of course!' both mean certainly

explanation.surface: A boundless pleasure, naturally, turns out to make someone rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a hoard of wealth, and a fortune is a large amount of money: synonyms.

clue.text: Private, one lacking energy to keep going

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

indicators.note: lacking means the word goes without a letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired private soldier, short of energy, has to keep marching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective but is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for persevering doggedly despite difficulty.

clue.text: Cambridge college keeping in touch from the start? Blow me!

indicators.note: keeping means the college holds the next word inside it

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University

indicators.note: from the start picks the opening letter of the word

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college stays in contact from the outset, and someone exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me!' is a British exclamation of surprise, but read literally it is what a clarinet asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument played by blowing, so it could say 'blow me'.

clue.text: Gullible type not hard to encounter, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: easy means not hard; to meet is to encounter

explanation.surface: A credulous person is said to be simple to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: EASY MEET sounds like the phrase, with MEAT spelled differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy meat is an idiom for a person who is readily fooled or defeated, a soft target.

clue.text: Appropriate American support so raised

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards

explanation.surface: A US prop is lifted in a fitting way.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is an adjective meaning relevant or fitting to the occasion, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Tag large murder victim

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
in Genesis, Abel was murdered by his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A tag is attached to a big murder victim, like a toe tag in a morgue.
explanation.definitionFit: A label and a tag are both small identifying tickets attached to things: synonyms.

clue.text: Start to describe posh English dance

indicators.note: to describe is to draw around, so the word encloses the next letter

parts.note: to begin is to start
U is the crossword letter for upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: Someone begins to describe a refined English dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something.
explanation.definitionFit: The beguine is a Caribbean ballroom dance, famous from Cole Porter's 'Begin the Beguine'.

clue.text: Pace street before getting lift

indicators.note: before puts the street ahead of the lift

parts.note: a lift is a ride, as in giving someone a lift

explanation.surface: Someone walks the street before getting a lift home.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a single long step, so a pace in the walking sense.

clue.text: Big blow to our sailors before a party

indicators.note: before puts the sailors ahead of 'a party'

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's (our) sailors
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A disaster strikes British sailors just ahead of a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big blow' reads like a setback but means a wind. 'Our sailors' is RN, the British Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, so a blow in the weather sense of a gale.

clue.text: Ready to drop everything, I note

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone is so exhausted they could drop everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop everything' reads as one phrase, but 'everything' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is British slang for utterly exhausted, so tired enough to collapse.

clue.text: Prompt start

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to provoke or cause, as a verb
second meaning: to set off or initiate, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning punctual, but here both words are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger an event is both to prompt it and to set it going, just as pulling a gun's trigger fires it.

clue.text: Troublemaker with the Spanish force

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker with Spanish help compels someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or compel them to act, a synonym for force as a verb.

clue.text: Diane, sort to provide amusement

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane
a version is a sort or kind of something

explanation.surface: Diane is asked to tidy things up to entertain everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like an anagram signal over Diane, but the letters do not fit; it means VERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a pastime that distracts and entertains, so a synonym for amusement.

clue.text: Gertrude ultimately learning about wrongdoing in Shakespearean setting

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the queen's name

parts.note: its last letter

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: lore is traditional learning
sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Gertrude, Hamlet's mother, finally learns of crimes in the castle where the play is set.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude is Hamlet's mother, which makes the Shakespearean setting feel part of the surface rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Hamlet takes place, the location of that tragedy.

clue.text: Disturbance not controlled? Not half!

indicators.note: not half says only half the word's letters are kept, the first six of twelve

parts.note: unrestrained means not controlled

explanation.surface: A riot gets out of hand, and the speaker emphatically agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'very much so', but here it removes half of UNRESTRAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is public agitation or discontent, a synonym for disturbance in the civil sense.
